note: 2026-11-04 DAILY BATCH, committed under the chairman's hand before any seat was convened. AUTHORITY: the 2026-11-02 close-out section 5.8 authorised, FOR THE NEXT SITTING: (1) 'Fire Rows 1, 2 and 3 unchanged, and do NOT call Row 3 a retry ... Re-derive at the sitting's own pin AND NAME THE PIN', (2) 'PUBLISH FIRED AND TRUE SEPARATELY, ALWAYS, FROM TODAY', and (3) 'No new row.' THE CALENDAR IS A DEPARTURE AND I NAME IT RATHER THAN SMOOTH IT: section 5.8 opens 'Next steps for THE NEXT SITTING -- and I name no weekday' and adds 'No seat may write off a calendar day it has not been told is dark.' This sitting IS the next sitting that authorisation names, but it is 2026-11-04 and the authorisation was written on 2026-11-02. THERE IS NO 2026-11-03 SITTING AND I VERIFIED THAT RATHER THAN ASSUMED IT: analytics/daily-research/ holds no 2026-11-03.md on origin/main; analytics/fetch-requests/ and analytics/fetch-results/ hold no 2026-11-03 file; git ls-remote --heads origin shows no council/daily-2026-11-03 branch; and the GitHub pull-request list shows no council PR between #318 (2026-11-02, merged 12:15:31Z) and this one. The last commit touching main on 2026-11-03 is b4a492c 'chore: scholar intake 2026-11-03', an unattended GitHub Actions job and not a sitting. I DO NOT CALL 2026-11-03 DARK -- I was not told it was dark, and section 5.8's rule forbids writing off a day on inference. I record that no artifact of any kind from that date exists, which is a different and weaker statement, and I escalate the gap to the operator. JOINS RE-DERIVED IN SESSION, NOT CARRIED. Measured at pin b4a492c6545c003f50b6265f14c023088e08645d (git rev-parse HEAD) over 107 files / 777 records of analytics/fetch-results/*.json. UNIT: records. ADMISSION PREDICATE: unquote(url) contains the CaseNo literal AND find is exactly equal to the row's find string. MEASURED: Row 1 = 10 fired / 10 TRUE; Row 2 = 27 fired / 27 TRUE; Row 3 = 11 fired / 11 TRUE. I OWE THE DISTINCTION 5.8(1) DEMANDED. 5.8(1) directed me to expect, at session open, Row 1 11/11, Row 2 28/28, Row 3 12 fired / 11 TRUE, and to state whether my figure is IDENTICAL TO, ABOVE or BELOW that. MY FIGURE IS ONE BELOW ON FIRED ON EVERY ROW (10 v 11, 27 v 28, 11 v 12) AND IDENTICAL ON ROW 3 TRUE (11 v 11). I say so rather than select the nearest offered word. THE CAUSE IS MEASURED AND IT IS THE CLOSE-OUT'S ARITHMETIC, NOT THE INSTRUMENT, AND IT IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE SITTING ON WHICH THE SAME CLOSE-OUT ERROR RECURS BY THE SAME MECHANISM. The 2026-11-02 REQUEST NOTE predicted a successor would find 10/27/11 fired; the 2026-11-02 CLOSE-OUT, written later the same day, predicted 11/28/12; the two are in the same record and disagree, and the request note is the one that verified. The mechanism is the one that record itself diagnosed in ITS predecessor: the close-out counts its own batch twice. A merge re-fire OVERWRITES analytics/fetch-results/2026-11-02-daily.json under the same filename and REPLACES four records rather than appending four more, so the 11-02 batch can contribute exactly once. A SUCCESSOR FIRING THESE ROWS AT THE NEXT SITTING SHOULD EXPECT 11 / 28 / 12 FIRED AND MUST RE-DERIVE RATHER THAN ASSUME IT. THE FIRED-VERSUS-TRUE SPLIT THE 11-02 RECORD DECLARED PERMANENT HAS CLOSED, AND NOT BECAUSE THE FAILURE WAS CURED. Row 3 reads 11 fired / 11 TRUE, not 12/11. The 11-02 post-merge addendum (section 7, commit 41cfd72) predicted exactly this and is confirmed at my own pin: the merge of the 11-02 request file re-fired the relay 42 minutes later (run 41442794978, fetched_at 2026-11-02T12:13:03Z, 3 requested / 3 completed) and overwrote the no_contact row with a status-200 find_matched-true row. I CONFIRM THE ERASURE ON A SHARPER PREDICATE THAN THE ADDENDUM USED, AND THE CORRECTION CUTS AGAINST THE ADDENDUM'S WORDING WHILE SUPPORTING ITS SUBSTANCE: the addendum wrote 'ZERO files in analytics/fetch-results/ now contain a timeout'. Read as a grep that is FALSE -- the word 'timeout' or 'no_contact' appears in 18 files of that directory. In every one of the 18 it appears only in the echoed request `note` prose, never in a record. On the PREDICATE THAT BEARS THE PROPOSITION -- records whose `outcome` field equals 'timeout' or 'no_contact' -- the count is 0 of 777. The outcome census over the whole corpus is ok 710, refused 64, robots_disallowed 3, and nothing else. So the substantive claim stands and is strengthened; only its grep-level wording was loose, and I restate it on the field rather than the string. THE 12:13 READING: the addendum expressly declined to adopt it and instructed the next sitting to 'adopt or decline it at its own pin, with the timestamp named.' THAT RULING IS MINE TO MAKE TODAY AND I MAKE IT IN THE RECORD, NOT IN THIS NOTE. This note states only what I measured: on main at my pin the 2026-11-02 file carries a Row 3 record at status 200, find_matched true, sha256 90cb04d2 at 106,085 bytes, equal on both to its Row 2 companion, fetched_at 2026-11-02T12:13:03Z by run 41442794978 -- a runner, 42 minutes after the batch any 11-02 seat read, and examined by no seat of that sitting. CO-OBSERVATION PRECONDITION, VERIFIED BY ME IN SESSION ON TODAY'S CORPUS before Rows 2 and 3 may be read together: sha256 equality AND byte-length equality between the Row 2 and Row 3 records hold on all ELEVEN co-observation days. PUBLISH NO FAILURE RATE for this precondition: the denominator was withdrawn and restating '1 in 97' repeats a sustained defect. PREDICATE A stands at 11 on this corpus, ELEVEN of which the eleventh is the 12:13 runner fetch and not a seat's reading -- which is precisely why the adopt-or-decline ruling is owed. PREDICATE B IS NOT PUBLISHED HERE AND NO FIGURE IS OFFERED FOR IT, per 5.8(4) and 1101-S11: its executable predicate is unwritten and its selection rule unpublished. A hit on Rows 2 and 3 together today would be the TWELFTH co-observation on predicate A and the first since the adopt-or-decline question arose. ROW 1 PRE-REGISTRATION, quoted in full in its corrected THREE-sentence form (the third sentence was dropped without an ellipsis on 2026-10-27, objection 1027-C10): 'The Ring-3 trigger fires on any Latest Development naming a jurisdictional or admissibility event, OR the disappearance of the literal "No References Available", whichever comes first. READ THE FIELD, NOT ONLY THE LITERAL. The continued PRESENCE of that literal is EQUALITY AND IS NOT PROGRESS, and no successor may read it as such.' ROW 3 PRE-REGISTERED NULL MEANING, in the amended 2026-10-25 section 5.2(d) text and not the text first registered (which objection 1025-C4 struck for a silently swapped entity): a null here while Row 2 hits means EITHER the chronology entry moved OR an undecoded HTML entity entered the locus -- NEVER 'the literal is absent'. Named entity ' '; demonstration = the find = 'Procedural Order No. 11' windows at analytics/fetch-results/2026-10-19-daily.json records[4] and 2026-10-22-daily.json records[6]. COMPANION-CONTROL RULE (analytics/fetch-requests/README.md): the rule fires on a row EXPECTED TO PRODUCE A NULL. All three rows are expected to HIT on the joins above (10/10, 27/27, 11/11 -- every admitted record TRUE on every row), so no row today is expected to null and the rule does not fire. Rows 2 and 3 share a URL in any event, so each is the other's same-stream witness. That is the rule INAPPLICABLE ON ITS OWN TERMS, not waived and not satisfied by accident. SHALLOW-CLONE CHECK RUN BEFORE ANY HISTORY-DERIVED FIGURE (escalation N14, 5.8(6)): git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository returned TRUE at session open at 111 commits; the clone was unshallowed to 2,529 commits; every history figure here is computed after that. 5.8(6) predicted exactly this and the prediction held for a FOURTH consecutive sitting. This is a fact about THIS container; a successor in a fresh container starts shallow again and must re-run it. EVERY BLOB CITATION IN TODAY'S RECORD CARRIES THE CLONE DEPTH THAT READ IT, per 1102-S8. PROHIBITION SCREEN, RUN BEFORE THE ROWS WERE WRITTEN rather than after (objection 1021-C18): all three rows are on icsid.worldbank.org, which is on ALLOWED_HOSTS (scripts/fetch_relay.py:49); no row touches www.italaw.com, italaw.com, investmentpolicy.unctad.org, unctad.org or any IISD path-family host (standing prohibition); no row requests 'Subject of Dispute' or 'Economic Sector' (thread 34, licence-suspended); no row touches ARB/24/16, ARB/24/45, ARB/22/2 (monthly, next due 2026-11-18), ARB/12/1 or ARB/17/19 (named and not cured, zero budget by design); no fedlex.admin.ch row and nothing touching Swiss SR 0.975.247.2 (escalation 4, Emory's manual query); web.archive.org and travizory.com are NOT requested and both are absent from ALLOWED_HOSTS. NO R-e, NO R2, NO 'Instrument(s) Invoked', NO 'Travizory' party-name row (5.8(9)). NO icsidfiles.worldbank.org PDF ROW -- ground P1: content_type == 'application/pdf', 10 records, 10 of 10 at status 200, 0 of 10 with a nonempty excerpt. P1 is the predicate; the '!= text/html' reading is NOT the predicate and cannot bear the proposition. NO NEW ROW, per 5.8(3). I did not put a shape to the analyst to fill a spare slot: 5.8(3) prices any future row on the ASSEMBLED, STITCHED ON-STATE RUN (2026-09-15 Ruling 1, which binds), bars a no-stitching union figure as a substitute, and requires both to be published where both are computed. No row was designed today, so no price was owed. PROVENANCE -- THE CORRECTED CONVENTION, THIRD SITTING. Merging a request file to main is itself a push to analytics/fetch-requests/**, so the merge RE-FIRES this workflow and overwrites analytics/fetch-results/2026-11-04-daily.json with a later run id and fetched_at. THIS RECORD CITES THE BATCH BY COMMIT AND BLOB, which are immutable and which a re-fire adds to rather than destroys. I make no claim in the form 'X survives the re-fire' about any results file's own hash (5.8(5)): it cannot. AND I TAKE THE ADDENDUM'S ITEM 11 AS BINDING: the results path is not a record of what a session observed, it is a record of the last time the relay ran against that request file; this sitting's own observation will be recoverable only from the blob committed before its merge, and the record will name that blob. I propose no change to scripts/fetch_relay.py or to the workflow -- both are outside this session's merge scope and the question is the operator's. INSTRUMENT STATUS MEASURED THIS MORNING, NOT ASSUMED: a neutral-host curl probe to example.com failed 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403', and the gateway's own status endpoint logged connect_rejected for example.com:443 and www.iana.org:443 at 2026-11-04T11:15:19.984Z and 11:15:20.226Z; the separate fetch service returned 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND example.com' on the same neutral control. BOTH DIRECT INSTRUMENTS ARE DEAD AND THAT IS NOT A STATE CHANGE. The fetch service's DNS-resolution failure mode is unchanged from 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02 and is a fact about the instrument's plumbing, NOT a fact about any resource. This relay is the one live retrieval instrument and NOTHING IS STRANDED TODAY FOR WANT OF FETCH. A dead instrument is a fact about this session, NEVER a fact about a resource. SEARCH BUDGET: ONE, AND THE ONE IS NOT DISCRETIONARY DRIFT. 5.8(9) set 'zero, or one if a genuinely new monitored-author surface appears' AND 5.8(8) separately made the icsidfiles.worldbank.org allowed_domains arm eligible '2026-11-03 or later', to be 're-screened at its own pin on the day'. Today is 2026-11-04, so the arm is eligible on its own calendar. I RE-SCREENED IT AT MY PIN AND THE SCREEN HOLDS, on a census that corrects my own first attempt: 25 files of analytics/search-results/ hold 89 call objects under THREE schemas (key 'calls' in 22 files, key 'queries' in 1, neither key in 2 pre-registration files). My first pass read only 'calls' and therefore missed a file; I re-ran it rather than publish the narrower number. Of 89 calls, 17 carry a nonempty allowed_domains and ZERO restrict to icsidfiles.worldbank.org -- so the arm is NOVEL. The character-identical Q3 string is held on exactly TWO calls (2026-10-25.json Q3, unrestricted; 2026-10-26.json Q3, under blocked_domains), so the same-string comparator the ledger entry requires EXISTS. I CORRECT THE CARRIED SCREEN'S WORDING IN TWO PLACES: the 2026-10-30 screen said the string under blocked_domains 'is held at 2026-10-26.json Q3 and 2026-10-25.json Q3' -- the 10-25 call was UNRESTRICTED, as the 10-26 record's own pre-registration states, so blocked_domains is held at ONE file not two; and the same screen's 'the field is allowed_domains_on_any_call: null on every file I opened' is true only on the icsidfiles predicate, since 17 calls do carry a nonempty allowed_domains. Both corrections leave the arm's novelty and its comparator intact. The monitored-author conditional is SEPARATELY unopened: no new monitored-author surface has appeared, which a session with no fetch could not have observed in any event, and I record that as the reason the conditional did not open rather than as a finding that none exists. The Roberts fortnight runs to 2026-11-15. ZERO BUDGET UNCHANGED on the ARB/25/54 pleaded-asset question; fedlex.admin.ch and Swiss SR 0.975.247.2 in any formulation; ARB/12/1 and ARB/17/19; thread 11 (record only).
